question: Your extraction system pulls fields from insurance claim forms into JSON that validates against your schema. The team compares two verifiers on the same 500 extracted records. The in-session verifier, a follow-up step in the extraction session, approves 98% of the records, while the independent verifier, a separate Claude instance that receives only the form and the JSON, flags 11% for wrong field values. Which conclusion should guide the team's choice of verifier?

options.text: Keep the in-session verifier, because the independent verifier lacks the extraction reasoning, so most of its additional flags are probably false positives.
options.reason: The guide states that review instances without prior reasoning context are more effective at catching subtle issues, so missing that context is an advantage, not a source of false positives.

options.text: Keep the in-session verifier and enable extended thinking for it, because deeper reasoning in the same session will match the independent verifier's detection rate.
options.reason: The guide states that independent review instances are more effective than extended thinking, because the same session still retains its own reasoning context.

options.text: Keep the in-session verifier, because every record already validates against the JSON schema, so a second instance adds cost without finding real errors.
options.reason: Schema validation checks structure, not whether the values are right; the errors flagged here are wrong field values that a valid schema does not catch.

options.text: Keep the independent verifier, because the extraction session retains its reasoning context and is less likely to question the field values it chose.
options.reason: A model that keeps its generation reasoning is less likely to question its own decisions, so the high approval rate reflects self-review bias, not accuracy.
